# **Best Practices for Screen Studio** 

## Self Recording & Demo Recording ---

 Last updated 11/26/2025

---

# **Overview**

Screen Studio is a great tool for improving our screen recordings. Unfortunately, it is currently only available for Mac. Anyone can download and record without a paid account. A license is only required for exporting.

If you’re recording a demo with LD’s video team you'll be responsible for setting up, testing, and running the Screen.Studio recording on your local machine.

---

# **🎥 Prefer watching over reading?**

# If you’d rather follow along with a video, check out this step-by-step walkthrough:

# **👉 [Video](https://f.io/57MsaUcH)**

# **Getting Started**

1. **Download** Screen Studio [**here**](https://www.screen.studio/download).   
2. Install the application on your computer.  
3. On first launch, grant both **recording** and **accessibility** permissions.  
4. **Restart your computer** after granting those permissions to ensure functionality.

---

# **Prepare to Record**

1. On your **Mac**, please **silence all notifications** or close apps like **Slack** and turn on **Do Not Disturb** in your calendar to avoid interruptions ahead of recording.  
2. Launch the Screen Studio app. You’ll see a toolbar on your screen like this:

![][image1]

3. By default, the **camera** and **mic** are OFF. **Turn both ON** and select the correct camera and mic (you may be prompted to allow access, grant access).

![][image2]  
![][image3]  
![][image4]

#### 

# **Recording Area Setup** *(Please read carefully\!)*

1. **SYSTEM SETTINGS:** A key consideration here is that we need the recording window to be at 1920x1080. Even higher is better but we need to stick to the 16x9 aspect ratio. On newer Mac laptops, you might have to go into **Settings \> Display**, and then change the display settings to **“More space”** in order to take full advantage of the screen resolution to get to 1920x1080. We normally discourage the use of external monitors because, in rare cases, they can add a delayed mouse-over effect in Screen.Stuido. But, if needed, we’ll use them to make sure we get to 1920x1080. 

   ![][image5]

2. **WINDOW RESIZER:**

   1. Download **[Window Resizer chrome plug-in](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/window-resizer/kkelicaakdanhinjdeammmilcgefonfh)**

   2. Using the **GREEN Task Bar** *(don’t select from the list of devices.)* Set the resolution to **1920x1080 \> Resize “window” \> click the arrow button**, the window size will automatically resize your browser window.

      

   

3. **CHROME SETTINGS:** *Appearance tab*

   1. **MODE SELECTION:**   
      **DARK MODE** \- is standard in 2026, but  
      **![][image6]**

      **LIGHT MODE** \- works too.  
      **![][image7]**

   2. **SHOW BOOKMARKS BAR:**  
      **![][image8]**  
        
4. **SCREEN.STUDIO ENABLE RECORDING:**  
1. Use **Window** mode on screen.studio to start recording. Click **"Window"** in the toolbar.  
   ![][image9]

2. Select the **Window** you would like to record. (*example: Chrome Browser*)   
   To start your recording by **clicking** on the purple start recording button.

   ![][image10]

**Please test these settings ahead of time.** If needed, the video team will work with you to make sure it’s all dialed in before your actual recording date.

For most demos, we record **a single app window** which captures the browser bar**:**

---

# **During Recording**

1. Click **Start Recording**.  
2. **Wait 3 seconds** before beginning your demo to allow the tool to start recording.  
3. Use the **timer/stop window** (small floating control box) to stop recording when done. **Click** the **Red Stop sign***.*  
    ![][image11]  
4. If you're also being recorded via Riverside, ensure the Screen Studio control is **not captured** in the video frame.

---

# **To Save**

1. Go to **File \> Save As**.  
2. Use a specific name (e.g., `John_Smith_Demo_10.9.24.screenstudio`).  
3. **Compress** the `.screenstudio` file  
4. Upload the `.screenstudio` file to your **LD Google Drive** or **send to the video team through Slack**.  
5. **Enable download access** and share with the video team.

| This is where your work ends\! The video team will receive your file, open your project, apply the LD Preset, adjust settings as needed, and export. Sending you back a hosted shared link. |
| :---- |

### **🎥 Recording Tips & Best Practices**

To help viewers follow your demo clearly and avoid re-recording later, here are a few helpful guidelines:

* **Use your cursor with intention**: Think of the cursor as a pointer. Move it smoothly and directly to the area you want to highlight. Pause slightly over important buttons or data points before clicking.

* **Hold after clicks**: After clicking a button or triggering an action, hold for **1–2 seconds** before moving the cursor. This gives viewers time to register the interaction.

* **Minimize unnecessary movement**: Avoid wiggling or looping the cursor around. Try to keep it within the recording window and use slow, deliberate gestures to guide attention.

* **Scroll with purpose**: If scrolling through a page, do it smoothly and slowly. Avoid fast or jerky scrolls that are hard to follow visually.

* **Narrate calmly and clearly**: Speak naturally and don’t rush. If you’re reading from a prompter, make sure your tone sounds conversational.

* **Keep your setup consistent**:

  * Use a **16” MacBook** if possible (or ensure screen size supports 1920x1080).

  * **Use a single built-in display** (avoid external monitors while recording).

  * **Close unnecessary apps**, browsers, or syncing programs to avoid lag.

  * Ensure at least **20GB of free disk space** before recording.

---

# **Conclusion**

That’s it\! That’s everything. Again, for most use cases, the video team will handle the project and export settings. But now you know our full process.  
If you run into any problems or roadblocks, please contact the video team.
